I am 76 years old and have farmed this land for 50 years. I only went to primary school, but I know farming from doing it every day and watching my father and neighbors. My farm is 16.1 mu, which is a good-sized piece of land in our village. I grow winter wheat and summer maize, rotating them every year.

Right now it is late April, and my wheat is growing well. I planted it last October using improved seed — not the old traditional kind, but the kind the seed dealer said was good and that my neighbor Wang used with success. Last autumn I ploughed the field deep and put down base fertilizer before planting: about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu. In March I topdressed with urea, and I just finished the jointing irrigation. In total I use about 20 kg of nitrogen per mu for wheat. I figure this from the bags: one 50-kg bag of compound fertilizer and almost one bag of urea per mu. I also get about 9 kg phosphorus and 5 kg potassium from the compound fertilizer. I will irrigate four times in total — the winter irrigation, the green-up irrigation, the jointing irrigation I just did, and one more at heading in May. I spray pesticide three times: herbicide in early spring, fungicide for rust, and insecticide for aphids. Last year I got 550 kg per mu, and I expect the same this year if no disaster comes.

After wheat harvest in early June, I will plant summer maize immediately. There is no time to waste. I use hybrid seed — everyone does now. I rotary till the stubble quickly because we must plant within a few days. For maize I use about 22 kg nitrogen per mu, 7 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium. I put base fertilizer when planting and topdress at the big ear stage. Maize needs more nitrogen than wheat because summer growth is fast. I irrigate three times: after planting, at big ear stage in July, and at grain filling in August. I spray pesticide three times. I expect 650 kg per mu.

My son works in the city and sends money home, but the farm still needs to produce. Fertilizer costs more now — urea is over 100 yuan per bag — but I never cut back. Last year my neighbor Chen tried to save 50 yuan per mu on fertilizer and his wheat turned yellow. He lost over 100 kg per mu. That taught me: better to waste a little fertilizer than lose yield. With 16 mu, if I lose 50 kg per mu, that is 800 kg total — a big loss. So I apply enough and sleep well. I watch my neighbors. If they apply more, I think about applying more too. Change is risky, so I mostly do what I did last year, adjusting only a little based on what I see in the fields.
